post.caption: Most rainbow moonstone is a different mineral. Moonstone is a feldspar with thin alternating layers inside, and light scatters off those layers in a glow called adularescence. That word comes from the Adula mountains in the Swiss Alps. A smooth dome cut, called a cabochon, shows the glow best, and the most prized stones are colorless with a blue sheen. Sri Lanka and India are two of its important sources. The Roman writer Pliny described a stone that held the moon's image, though it is unclear whether he meant moonstone. Moonstone is one of the modern June birthstones. Rainbow moonstone is usually labradorite, a different feldspar.
